helpIntro: Find a comfortable breathing rhythm that works for you.
helpChooseBody: Choose Coherent Breathing, Box Breathing, 4-7-8 or Custom on Settings, or explore the practice library for more rhythms.
helpAdjustBody:
Set the duration of each phase: inhale, hold, exhale and hold.

You can adjust the timing in 0.5-second increments. Set either hold to 0 if you prefer continuous breathing without pauses.
helpLengthBody:
Select how long you would like to practice.

The app always finishes a complete breathing cycle, so a few extra seconds may be added to your selected session length.
helpStartBody:
Tap Start Practice.

You will have three silent seconds to gently breathe out before the session begins.

Then follow the movement of the water and the sounds at a comfortable pace.
helpImportantBody:
Breathing should feel natural, comfortable and gentle.

There is no need to force a deep inhale, push the air out or hold your breath longer than feels comfortable.

You can shorten the breathing times, remove the holds or return to your natural breathing at any moment.

The goal is not perfect performance. It is to discover a breathing rhythm that feels right for you.
offlineSaving: Saving the app, photos and sounds for offline use…

adjustedRhythm: Your adjusted rhythm keeps this practice selected.
equalPhasesHint: All four phases use the same duration. Shorten them to stay comfortable.
ratioHint: Inhale : exhale = 1:{ratio}. The exhale is calculated automatically.
adjustComfort: Use a shorter rhythm whenever you need. Choose Custom Breathing on Home to adjust every phase independently or remove holds.
comfortSafety: Keep breathing gentle and comfortable. If you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, return to your natural breathing.
holdCaution: Holds are optional. Shorten or skip them if they feel uncomfortable; never strain to follow the suggested pattern.
coherentShort: An even, unhurried rhythm without holds.
coherentExplanation: Breathe in and out for the same length, with no pauses. The suggested 5.5-second rhythm is a starting point, not a target to achieve.
coherentBenefit: An even rhythm may support a steadier focus on breathing. A comfortable pace matters more than matching a number.
coherentUse: Can be used for a quiet break, a transition between activities, or a few minutes of attentive breathing.
boxShort: Four equal phases, including gentle holds.
boxExplanation: Follow four equal phases: inhale, hold, exhale, hold. Adjust their common duration together.
boxBenefit: The repeating structure offers a clear anchor for attention. Some people find the predictable rhythm useful for settling into a task.
boxUse: May fit a short pause before a focused activity, when brief holds feel easy and comfortable.
equalShort: Equal inhale and exhale, at your own pace.
equalExplanation: Choose an inhale duration and let the exhale match it. There are no holds. Begin with 4.5 seconds, or choose a shorter pace.
equalBenefit: A simple, even rhythm can support attention and presence. It does not need to be fast, and the ratio does not guarantee stimulation.
equalUse: Can be used during a daytime break or when you want a gentle return to the present moment.
extendedShort: A gentle exhale twice as long as the inhale.
extendedExplanation: Choose an inhale duration; the exhale is twice as long. Leave out holds and let the breath stay light.
extendedBenefit: A longer, easy exhale may help some people slow their pace. Shorten the inhale if the resulting exhale feels too long.
extendedUse: May fit an evening pause or a moment of slowing down. Return to an equal or natural rhythm whenever that is easier.
478Explanation: The suggested pattern is 4 seconds in through the nose, a 7-second hold, and 8 seconds out gently through the mouth. Adapt every phase to comfort.
478Benefit: A defined sequence can give attention a steady structure. The hold is optional; the numbers are not a test or a promise of an outcome.
478Use: Can be explored during a quiet break if longer phases feel comfortable. Choose a shorter pattern or remove the hold as needed.
helpSafetyBody:
Do not practice breathing exercises while driving, diving, or engaging in any activity where changes in concentration or physical sensations could put you or others at risk.

If you experience discomfort, dizziness, weakness, or distress during practice, stop the exercise. Seek professional advice when appropriate.

The breathing exercises in this app are intended for personal well-being and relaxation and are not a substitute for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
